messages.subject: [unmarked] syntax question
parts:
Hi, I was wondering if you could help me with something very simple. I am trying to run a two species occupancy model and I am working through the example in the unmarked vignette.

In the example, this is what is listed for the state and detection processes. However, I don't understand what exactly goes in each one. The example says '~par1' for example.

# Formulas for state and detection processes

# Length should match number/order of columns in fDesign
occFormulas <- c('~par1','~par2','~par3','~1','~1','~1','~1')

#Length should match number/order of species in data@ylist
detFormulas <- c('~1','~1','~1') #3 species: coyote, tiger, bear

Thanks !!

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] syntax question
parts:
I'm not exactly sure what you're asking but I'll give it a shot.

In the example occFormulas is a character vector with one entry/formula for each natural (f) parameter in the model.
So for the first natural parameter f1 the formula is '~par1' , meaning f1 is a function of  covariate "par1" (which is the name of a variable in the data) plus an intercept.
If you need help with what the f parameters represent I suggest looking at Chris Rota's 2016 paper ("A multispecies occupancy model for two or more interacting species" in Methods in Ecology and Evolution).

For detFormulas each entry is also a formula, corresponding to the detection model for each species in the analysis.
So the first entry is the detection model  for species 1, and it's an intercept only model ("~1"). The detection models for all three species are intercept only models in this example.

messages.author: 75100463b7eff618
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] syntax question
parts:
I *think* the detFormulas syntax gives the detection function for each species. So the example is saying there is a different detection probability for each of the  three species.
So for two species it would just be
detFormuals <- c('~1','~1')
For the occFormulas, there should be  (2^n) -1  parameters.
The syntax (I think) gives the first order ones ( one for each species), then the second order ones (i.e. difference in log odds occupancy of species s occurring when another species is present and absent.) And third order if there are three species. etc
So for two species it should just be 
occFormulas <- c('~par1','~par2','~1')
(In the example I think they are giving covariates for occupancy for each species (par1, par2 etc)

If you want a model that ignores the species interactions I think you can set the values to 0.
e.g.
occFormulas <- c('~par1','~par2','~par3','~0','~0','~0','~0')
Which will be like fitting three separate occupancy models

Not sure if this helps - someone can jump in and correct anything here - I have a lot of "I think" statements!

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] syntax question
parts:
e.g.


The following specification in the example:
> occFormulas <- c('~1','~1','~1','~0','~0','~0','~0')

> fit <- occuMulti(detFormulas,occFormulas,data)
> 
> #Look at output
> fit


will just have a species occupancy and detection for each species without covariates and no dependence between species. - So an intercept only model

e.g. results are:
